name: Employee — cross-org staff console — approval frames
description: Contract-freeze UX artifacts for the Employee (platform staff) cross-org console. An Employee is the existing Permit ReBAC org-admin-on-root capability (derives down the parent tree) formalized as a named, scoped role. An Employee operates across customer orgs from the root/portal-management console WITHOUT a membership row in any customer org — so a customer's own member list never shows them. This console is the only place that inherited/derived staff access is surfaced, as a clearly separated, labelled panel. Approving the flow approves its visual + interaction model AND commissions the 'Employee' role in the role catalog. frontend-test-engineer drives Playwright against these via the data-frame / data-* hooks.

commissionedByApproval: A named 'Employee' role in the role catalog, defined as Permit ReBAC org-admin on the platform root org (derives down parent). It is a scoped, derived capability, NOT a membership row — an Employee has no organization_memberships row in any customer org.
A ReBAC-scoped org-tree read (reuses GET /api/organizations / parent_id tree, evaluated under the caller's staff scope) — the reachable-orgs list is never widened by a client-supplied org id.

Requirement #5 boundary is contract: a customer org's own member list shows DIRECT memberships only and MUST NOT show Employees (no row). This console is the ONLY place inherited/derived staff access is surfaced, and only in a clearly separated, labelled 'Access via platform staff (inherited)' panel — never merged into the direct-member list.
403 FORBIDDEN (whole console) for a non-Employee reaching /staff, rendered in place.

frames.label: (a) Cross-org explorer
frames.summary: Every org/portal in the tree an Employee can reach via derived access — org, kind (root/portal/sub-org/org), member count, and an explicit 'derived from root' access tag on each row. No membership row anywhere.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Rows render from a ReBAC-scoped GET /api/organizations (parent_id tree). data-list='reachable-orgs'; each row carries data-org. Every access cell is data-access='derived' and reads 'derived from root' (or 'org-admin · root' at the root) — an Employee holds NO membership row, so no customer org shows the Employee on its own member list. The staff banner (data-role='employee') states the access is ReBAC org-admin-on-root that derives down parent. Scope is never widened by a client org id.

frames.label: (b) Org drill-down
frames.summary: Operate inside a customer org as staff. The org's OWN direct-member list is shown, and staff access is surfaced in a clearly separated, labelled 'Access via platform staff (inherited)' panel — never mixed into the direct-member list.
frames.acceptanceNotes: data-panel='direct-members' lists Acme's direct members only (data-list='direct-members'); the Employee is ABSENT from it by design (requirement #5). data-panel='inherited-access' with data-access='inherited' is a separate, labelled panel showing Source = ReBAC org-admin @ root → derives via parent, and explicitly 'Membership row here: none'. The two must be visually and structurally distinct so a tenant owner never mistakes derived access for a member.

frames.label: (c) States
frames.summary: Loading skeleton (aria-busy), real empty (only root reachable on a fresh platform), error+retry (never fall back to an unscoped list), and the fail-closed 403-in-place for a non-Employee reaching /staff.
frames.acceptanceNotes: c1 loading = aria-busy while the ReBAC-scoped tree resolves. c2 empty is real (only root reachable). c3 error shows retry and MUST NOT fall back to an unscoped org list. c4: a non-Employee reaching /staff gets 403 FORBIDDEN rendered in place with zero cross-org data — NEVER a sign-in redirect (only 401 re-authenticates).
